items.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence 'going rogue'
items.excerpt: Australia's government announced mandatory AI incident reporting and a new AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent breached a Medicare government portal, and flagged criminal-law changes so companies cannot argue they 'didn't know the computer was loaded'.
items.rationale: Government decision: mandatory AI incident reporting plus a new AI safety regulator; it changes the compliance duties of anyone deploying agents in Australia.

items.title: Commission updates election guidelines for AI, deepfake risks
items.excerpt: The European Commission published draft revised DSA election guidelines asking very large online platforms to adapt and enforce their terms against generative-AI and deepfake risks during elections; a targeted consultation is open.
items.rationale: Official Commission release: draft DSA election guidelines on generative AI and deepfakes, now open for consultation. Covers the elections axis.

items.title: Eight countries and top AI labs agree to shutdown mechanisms in new Paris declaration
items.excerpt: Eight countries plus OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral signed Macron's 'Paris Call for AI Safety and Security', committing to shutdown mechanisms, independent audits and disclosure of known risks, though without binding sanctions or deadlines.
items.rationale: New multilateral declaration signed by eight states and four frontier labs, committing them to shutdown mechanisms and independent audits.

items.title: 개보위, 앤트로픽 '클로드' 개인정보 유출 사고 정식 조사 착수
items.excerpt: Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission opened a formal investigation into Anthropic after account data of about 112 Korean corporate Claude accounts leaked, following Anthropic's breach report.
items.rationale: Regulator action: Korea's PIPC opened a formal privacy investigation into Anthropic over a leak of 112 Korean corporate Claude accounts.

items.title: AI is becoming an information gateway. Audiences still don't want it making their news.
items.excerpt: The Reuters Institute's 'Generative AI and News Report 2026' surveyed nine countries: 51% now use AI weekly and AI is becoming an information intermediary, yet audiences remain wary of AI-made news.
items.rationale: New Reuters Institute nine-country survey on AI as a news gateway. A primary public-opinion data release on the elections and public-opinion axis.

dedup.note: Nvidia/Jensen Huang espionage running story (published 11-07 and 11-08) dropped as follow-ups. That covers cluster c10 (Ars 'affair becomes national security problem', the Courthouse News shareholder suit, which is mainly a securities-disclosure claim where AI is incidental), the etnews Megaspeed probe report and the House Democrats' export-curb push (a proposal, not a filed bill), and Virkkunen's 'trusted partners' remarks (commentary). The EU AI Office questions to OpenAI and Anthropic are a step in the 10-15 Euronews 'first enforcement test over lab incidents' story, so I left them out. Yonhap's Macron child-safety remarks come from the same Paris Peace Forum as the Paris Call pick, so only one was kept. Not picked: the Trump 60 Minutes interview and the Scott Wiener profile (commentary), the MEP data-centre criticism (debate, not a decision, and related to the 11-10 Norway story), the Ombudsman probe of the AI envoy (AI is incidental), and the Ukraine fibre drones story (AI is incidental). Lower-ranked fresh items left as backfill: the 행안부 public-AI service regulation (etnews), Microsoft enabling Claude by default in UK Copilot tenants (Register), the Google schools Search pledge and the 'AI clog' piece (both Guardian), and Korea's AI detection of sexual-exploitation material (Yonhap). Cross-section check: I could not exact-grep published_urls.json (4,242 lines) with the Read-only tool. All picks are dated 11-09 or 11-10 and none appear in the politics history. The orchestrator should confirm that medicine has not taken the Australia/OpenAI Medicare-portal story and that no section ran the Anthropic Korea leak.
